The petitioner is the sole accused in Crime No.1349/2023 of Thrikkodithanam Police Station,
Kottayam District, alleging commission of offences under Sections 376 (2)(n) and 354 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. Petitioner is working as a cashier at the Mahadeva Temple, Thengana, Kottayam district.

The allegation against the petitioner is that after befriending the defacto complainant/victim and after giving her a false promise of marriage the petitioner engaged in sexual relationships with her and thereafter withdrew from the promise of marriage and thereby he committed the offences alleged against him.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the allegations against the petitioner are totally false.
It is submitted that the alleged victim was used to frequent the temple (in which the petitioner is working as a cashier) and used to project herself as a cancer patient and a single mother.
It is submitted that on feeling sympathy for the defacto complainant/victim, the petitioner arranged for some money to be collected in order to help the defacto complainant/victim with her treatment.

It is submitted that thereafter it was learnt that the defacto complainant/victim was in the habit of collecting money form different places by giving false stories about herself and therefore the petitioner stopped helping the defacto complainant/victim.
It is submitted that thereafter false allegations of rape and promise to marry etc. have been raised against the petitioner.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor refers to the First Information Statement of the defacto complainant/victim and contends that there are allegations which would show that the offences alleged against the petitioner are attracted.
It is submitted that the matter is under investigation and a clear picture will be available only after the investigation is completed.
It is submitted that the allegations, if true, are serious.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioner, in reply, would submit that the petitioner has been in custody for 45 days and further detention of the petitioner may not be necessary for the purposes of investigation.
He submits that he will co-operate with the investigation in every manner and that he will also abide by any condition that will be imposed while granting bail to him.
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor, I am of the opinion that the petitioner can be granted bail subject to conditions.
No criminal antecedents are reported against the petitioner.
The petitioner has been in custody for 45 days.
The continued detention of the petitioner is not shown to be necessary for the purposes of completing the investigation.
8. In the result this bail application is allowed.
